title: Rectangular invariance and zero padding
subtitle: G2 lecture 059000 · expanded companion
adaptation: Standalone slide treatment of the spoken lecture and display-only mathematical appendix; authored derivations, worked calculations and local SVG diagrams.

slides.title: The same map inside a larger space
slides.lead: Adding an output coordinate that is always zero should not change any standard singular-value measurement.
body: Take A:ℝ²→ℝ³ with columns (4,0,0) and (0,2,0). Its singular values are (4,2). Embed the outputs isometrically in ℝ⁴ by appending a zero coordinate.
The resulting map has a new matrix shape but exactly the same nonzero action. The correct cross-dimensional norm convention keeps its size unchanged.
slides.takeaway: Isometric codomain embedding leaves the source Gram operator unchanged.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · The same map inside a larger space

slides.title: Prove output padding with a Gram identity
slides.lead: Let J:F→G be a linear isometry, so J*J=I on F.
body: The source Gram operator of JA is A*J*JA, which simplifies to A*A. As Gram eigenvalues determine the singular values, JA and A have identical singular values, including multiplicity.
This proof works for rectangular A because both Gram operators act on the same input space E. It avoids any coordinate-level argument about inserting zero rows.
slides.takeaway: Equal source Gram operators give equal singular values.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · Prove output padding with a Gram identity

slides.title: What changes when we enlarge the source?
slides.lead: Let I:E→H embed the input space isometrically into a larger space.
body: Extend A to H by first projecting onto I(E) and identifying that component with E, then applying A. Algebraically this is A I*, where I* is zero on the orthogonal complement of I(E).
On the enlarged source, the Gram operator has the old Gram block plus a zero block. Hence the nonzero singular values stay the same and extra zero singular values appear.
slides.takeaway: Input padding adds kernel directions, not new stretching.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · What changes when we enlarge the source?

slides.title: See the same fact through the SVD
slides.lead: A singular-value decomposition already isolates all nonzero stretching directions.
body: Enlarging the codomain leaves the output singular vectors embedded in a bigger orthonormal family. Enlarging the domain adds orthogonal input directions on which the extended map vanishes.
The nonzero stretch factors are unchanged in both constructions. This supplies a geometric explanation of the Gram calculation.
slides.takeaway: Padding changes available coordinate directions but not the nonzero SVD factors.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · See the same fact through the SVD

slides.title: A numerical padded matrix
slides.lead: The three-by-two map with diagonal entries four and two has Gram operator diag(16,4).
body: Appending an all-zero fourth output row does not change that two-by-two Gram matrix. Appending a zero input column creates a three-by-three source Gram matrix diag(16,4,0).
Both padded maps retain singular values four and two, with the extra zero visible only if the singular-value list convention includes the enlarged domain.
slides.takeaway: Zero padding preserves nonzero Gram eigenvalues and adds only zeros.

slides.title: A warning about dimension-dependent normalization
slides.lead: Unitarily invariant norms defined separately for each shape need not agree under padding.
body: For example, multiply the Frobenius norm on m-by-n matrices by a shape-dependent factor c_(m,n)>0. Each resulting norm remains unitarily invariant on its own matrix space.
But adding a zero row changes the factor when c_(m+1,n) differs from c_(m,n). The padded matrix then acquires a different size despite having the same singular values.
slides.takeaway: Fixed-shape unitary invariance does not force a coherent padding convention.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · A warning about dimension-dependent normalization

slides.title: Padding and compression are different operations
slides.lead: Appending zero coordinates leaves every existing output unchanged; projecting away a nonzero component does not.
body: If Q is an orthogonal projection on the output space, QA generally has smaller output lengths than A on some inputs. Its source Gram matrix is A*QA, a positive operator bounded above by A*A.
That comparison yields singular-value inequalities, not equality in general. Calling this “padding” would erase the essential loss of information.
slides.takeaway: Zero extension preserves singular values; orthogonal compression may decrease them.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · Padding and compression are different operations

slides.title: Isometric changes in both directions
slides.lead: Coordinate change is a special case of moving the same linear map through isometries.
body: Output embeddings preserve the Gram operator exactly. Input embeddings, followed by adjoints, add zero kernel directions. Standard gauge families such as Schatten norms ignore those extra zeros.
This is the cross-space counterpart of unitary invariance and is the correct hypothesis to use when writing estimates for rectangular residual maps.
slides.takeaway: A consistent Schatten gauge ignores added orthogonal zero directions.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · Isometric changes in both directions

slides.title: Why subspace perturbation uses this
slides.lead: A residual often maps a small trial space into a much larger ambient space.
body: Its meaningful singular values should not depend on whether it is represented using a basis of the ambient space or an isometrically embedded output block. Likewise, extra source coordinates that the residual kills should contribute only zeros.
Explicit padding compatibility lets us transfer estimates between block coordinates and whole-space operators without changing the measured quantity.
slides.takeaway: Rectangular invariance makes norm comparisons independent of ambient embedding choices.
slides.eyebrow: G2 · 059000 · Why subspace perturbation uses this

slides.title: Rebuild both Gram calculations
slides.lead: Compute the effect of an isometric embedding on both the input and output sides.
body: For JA, use J*J=I to show equality of Gram matrices. For AI*, identify the old Gram operator on I(E) and the zero operator on its orthogonal complement.
Then compare with compression A*QA, and exhibit a case where compression strictly reduces a singular value.
slides.takeaway: The Gram operator distinguishes exact padding invariance from contractive compression.
